Middle East.headline: Fact-checking Trump's speech at the United Nations General Assembly
Middle East.body: Donald Trump's UN address was packed with claims that are misleading, false or exaggerated. He said the US has more munitions than it could ever use, despite reports of depleting stocks. He also claimed the US and Venezuela hold 60 percent of the world's oil, despite the numbers not adding up, and he said he had ended the war in Gaza despite ongoing Israeli strikes and deaths since last year's ceasefire. Vedika Bahl fact-checks the speech in Truth or Fake.

Middle East.headline: Seafarer Killed in Hormuz Attack as Trump Pushes Iran Deal at UN
Middle East.body: An Indian seafarer has been killed after the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier Cape Dao was attacked and abandoned near the Strait of Hormuz, adding to a mounting casualty toll as the United States and Iran reopen diplomatic contacts at the United Nations. The Cape Dao was targeted about 2.5 nautical miles from Oman’s Musandam Governorate on Wednesday, according to Oman’s Maritime Security Center. The attack sparked a fire in the engine room, and a Royal Navy of Oman vessel evacuated 27 surviving crew members and provided medical care. One crew member was killed. UK Maritime Trade Operations had earlier reported that the cargo vessel was struck by an unknown projectile at around 0630

Middle East.headline: Yemeni forces say they repel Houthi attacks in Taiz as fighting rages
Middle East.body: Yemeni forces say they repel Houthi attacks in Taiz as fighting rages. Government forces say dozens of Houthis killed in southwestern governorate during battles for strategic highlands.

Americas.headline: Mexico — Hurricane Polo threatens southwestern coast
Americas.body: Residents along Mexico's southwestern Pacific coast are preparing for heavy rain, dangerous surf, severe flooding, and mudslides as Hurricane Polo tracks northwestward offshore. The Category 4 storm is churning near coastal beach towns, presenting significant hazards to southwestern communities. Elsewhere in the Pacific basin, another storm system, Nolo, is approaching Hawaii.

Americas.headline: Venezuela — UN address highlights recovery from twin earthquakes and crisis
Americas.body: Addressing the United Nations General Assembly, Acting President Delcy Rodríguez declared that Venezuela is working to rebuild following severe political crisis and natural disasters. Rodríguez cited a diplomatic dispute with the United States and a devastating twin earthquake that struck on 24 June 2026 as major national trials, while emphasizing ongoing recovery efforts across the country.

Africa.headline: DR Congo Ebola outbreak toll exceeds 3,700 deaths
Africa.body: DR Congo Ebola outbreak toll exceeds 3,700 deaths More than 130 days into the latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), health experts said on Wednesday that response efforts have been scaled up significantly and “the first encouraging signs of progress” are now being seen. In an update, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said that in the last 21 days, cases of infection fell by approximately 26 per cent in province of Ituri and by 15 per cent in the province of Haut Uele. Africa.headline: Nigeria Raises Ebola Alert as Deadly Outbreak Spreads Massively in DR Congo
Africa.body: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has raised the alarm over the ongoing Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), placing Nigeria on heightened alert. In a health advisory signed by its Director-General, Jide Idris, the agency said it had begun precautionary measures to strengthen the country’s preparedness and ensure a swift response should the disease pose a threat to Nigeria. The NCDC said the measures would be regularly reviewed as the situation develops and as new public health risks emerge. Europe.headline: Ukraine — Russian Strikes Kill Eight, Target Civilian Infrastructure
Europe.body: Recent Russian ballistic missile and drone attacks killed eight people across Ukraine, according to official reports. Strikes killed two individuals in Kyiv and six at an agricultural facility in the Kharkiv region, while a maternity clinic was also damaged. The strikes come as Ukrainian civilians prepare for winter amidst escalating Russian bombardment targeting critical energy infrastructure across the country.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — UN Officials and Coalition of 50 States Call for Ceasefire
Europe.body: UN Under-Secretary-General Rosemary DiCarlo called for an immediate, full, and unconditional ceasefire in Ukraine during a Security Council briefing on rising civilian risks. Additionally, a coalition of over 50 UN member states delivered a joint statement urging Moscow to accept an immediate ceasefire and return to peace negotiations. Moscow rejected the appeal. Concurrently, the United States and Russia engaged in talks during the UN General Assembly focused on reducing the conflict's impact on global energy.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Floods, Hunger and Disease Pile on Myanmar’s Civil War Misery
Asia-Pacific.body: Floods, Hunger and Disease Pile on Myanmar’s Civil War Misery YANGON, Myanmar, September 23 (IPS) - Isolated and at constant war with itself, Myanmar’s humanitarian crisis is deepening as global challenges far exceed the capacity to respond of a military regime increasingly focused on its own survival. The climate crisis, soaring commodity prices triggered by wars in Europe and the Middle East, plus worldwide cuts in donor aid are all hitting Myanmar hard. The regime’s inability to govern a fragmented and restive country with nearly four million internally displaced people has been exposed to the full since it seized power over five years ago. Asia-Pacific.headline: Rohingya refugees deserve a future beyond survival, not endless displacement
Asia-Pacific.body: This article is published in association with United Nations. Nine years after the mass displacement of the Rohingya from Myanmar, their situation remains one of the world’s most protracted and complex refugee crises, marked by years of persecution and uncertainty over the prospect of returning home. Against this backdrop, senior UN officials on Wednesday renewed calls for a durable solution that would enable Rohingya refugees to return home safely and with dignity, while ensuring justice and accountability. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: David Miliband: Aid cuts to blame for Ebola outbreak that has killed thousands
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Former foreign secretary David Miliband has denounced "bloody frustrating" cuts in overseas aid by the Labour government. Claims that such aid spending is a waste of money makes him want to "scratch my fingernails on the chalk board" in exasperation, he says. In an exclusive interview with The Independent, Mr Miliband, who runs the US based International Rescue Committee aid organisation, also fiercely criticises cuts in aid by Donald Trump. In a wide ranging discussion with The Independent Editor-in-Chief Geordie Greig, he said the cuts are to blame for the outbreak of the deadly Ebola disease in Africa which has claimed more than 3,000 lives since May. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: US releases additional US$267mil to combat Ebola outbreak
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: “To date, the United States government has provided US$887 million in direct health and humanitarian assistance to combat the Ebola outbreak,” the US state department said in a statement, adding that Washington was the largest aid provider for the latest outbreak. The aid announcement, made on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, also seeks to “call on capable nations to increase burden sharing to meet the urgency of the moment,” the statement said. Outgoing UN secretary-general Antonio Guterres last month issued an appeal to raise an additional $1.1 billion in aid against the epidemic, which continues to spread to new parts of the DRC, according to the NGO Doctors Without Borders (MSF)
